questions.name: Question 16
questions.question: Paint is sold in two sizes at a local shop. • Four-litre cans at $90 per can • Ten-litre cans at $205 per can Mina needs to purchase 80 litres of paint. Calculate the amount of money Mina will save by purchasing only ten-litre cans of paint rather than only four-litre cans of paint.

questionContent.text: Paint is sold in two sizes at a local shop. • Four-litre cans at $90 per can • Ten-litre cans at $205 per can Mina needs to purchase 80 litres of paint. Calculate the amount of money Mina will save by purchasing only ten-litre cans of paint rather than only four-litre cans of paint.

questions.answer:
Use the NESA marking criteria and sample answer below. Accept equivalent correct reasoning and working, valid follow-through and appropriate rounding. Only credit evidence present in the response.

• Provides correct solution 2
• Finds the cost of ten-litre cans, or equivalent merit 1
Sample answer:
Cost of ten-litre cans: $205 × 8
= $1640
Cost of four-litre cans: $90 × 20
= $1800
Savings = $1800 − $1640
= $160
